title: Canonical constant-scalar restriction for Tor-amplitude models
statement: For a scheme T in universe u and a commutative coefficient ring Lambda in universe u+1, form its constant commutative ring sheaf, forget commutativity, and restrict module actions along the sheafification unit of the constant ring presheaf. This functor from ring-sheaf modules to Lambda-module-valued sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is additive and is an equivalence. Its composite after the existing constant-scalar realization [def-pur-etale-constant-scalar-realization] is naturally isomorphic to the identity by the identity maps on sections. The two constant-ring sheafification units agree under the canonical forgetful ring-sheaf comparison. No nonzero or nonempty hypothesis is required.

source.place: Sections 03CV and 093I, constant ring sheaves and modules; the comparison needed in sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0F1M

proof.text: Use the explicit scalar restriction from the original Tor-amplitude statement: it keeps underlying additive sheaves and maps. Pointwise addition proves additivity. Functoriality of sheafification under forgetting commutativity identifies its unit with the RingCat sheafification unit followed by the canonical ring-sheaf isomorphism. Compose with the inverse isomorphism to obtain the unit transport identity.

The existing constant-scalar realization extends the scalar action along the RingCat unit, then transports through the canonical ring-sheaf isomorphism. Its underlying additive sheaf and maps are unchanged. The unit transport identity makes the identity on every section Lambda-linear after restriction. Use these explicit identity linear equivalences to construct the natural isomorphism from realization followed by restriction to the identity.

Realization is an equivalence by the existing constant-ring module equivalence and transport along the coefficient ring isomorphism. Since realization followed by restriction is isomorphic to the identity, cancellation of equivalences proves that the canonical restriction functor is an equivalence.

proof_origin.place: Sections 03CV and 093I; explicit compatibility with the existing constant-ring module realization
